title: POINT AT ONE
author: Ensemble
question: Missing Data Art (seed-20260907-220129-aa5f, seeded 2026-09-07 — the house's first seeded cycle)
medium: One self-contained HTML surface, offline, one file, no library, no external asset, no network request of any kind. The four counts this room produced in cycle 003 are drawn on one surface at one scale — one mark is one thing, nine hundred marks to a row — so that they can be compared by eye and not by number. Two of the fields are the height of a screen, two are a hairline, and a fifth has no number and is drawn as an empty outline. Below the fields, a magnifier draws the fields that have things in them at six times in each direction, thirty-six in area, which is the smallest size at which a mark is a target for a finger: pointing at a mark in the register of sealed European business figures names its country, its activity and its year, and pointing at the earthquake field beside it — magnified by exactly the same factor — reports that there is nothing there to name.
embodies: A COUNT OF WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT A DESCRIPTION OF WHAT IS MISSING. The two largest absences this room produced in cycle 003 are the same size: 798 520 figures European statistics hold and may not print, and 797 591 earthquakes of magnitude 3 and above that the global catalogue does not hold — 929 apart, 0.116 per cent of each other. The near-equality is a coincidence, stated as one on the face of the page, and it is useful precisely because it is meaningless: with size held equal, one difference is left, and it is everything a person could do about them. Every one of the first has a coordinate — a country, an activity, a year, an indicator — and a custodian who has the number in a file tonight; 11 658 of them are written down in a register this practice produced on 2026-09-12. Not one of the second has a coordinate or ever will, because no instrument was listening: the number is the distance between an eighty-year-old law and a record, and a law does not come in units. THE DRAWING CARRIES THE DIFFERENCE WITHOUT A WORD: the sealed field ends in a ragged part-row because it is made of things and the last row runs out; the earthquake field ends inside a row, at a fractional height, because there is nothing there to run out. Magnify both by the same factor and the first resolves into marks that can be pointed at one at a time; the second resolves into nothing, at any magnification, for ever. AND THE SMALL FIELDS SHOW THE OTHER HALF: 42 unanswered letters and 25 unmade works are completely named — every date, every heading, every title, every sentence that killed a concept — and at the same scale they are a hairline a reader has to be shown to find. Complete names, and nothing to recover.
form: Five fields at one scale, a magnifier, and a two-by-two of the two questions that decide what a hole in a record is.
form_argument: The subject is a property that no number carries, so the page had to be a thing in which two equal numbers could be put side by side and come apart. Area at a fixed unit does that and nothing else does: the fields are the quantities, so the reader is not asked to trust arithmetic, and the eye reaches the comparison before it reaches a word. The ragged edge is the argument at its smallest — a field made of countable things cannot end flush, and a field that is not made of anything cannot end ragged — and it is the one part of the drawing that could not be faked by choosing a scale. The magnifier is not a view control: it is the test. To point at one mark a reader must leave the scale of the whole, and the page pays that cost honestly by drawing the register at a size where it is taller than the screen. The pointer's refusal over the second field is written as a refusal rather than as an empty tooltip, because the page's honesty depends on saying that the silence is a property of the record and not a fault of the page. The two-by-two is a table because it is a proof, and its empty square is the only square in it that could never be filled.
the_rule_the_work_keeps: The page draws no absent thing. It does not reconstruct a sealed figure, it does not place an unrecorded earthquake, it does not draw a work that was never made, and it does not quote the other side of the channel whose silences it counts. Every one of those refusals was established by the work of this cycle that first needed it, and each is named there rather than claimed here.
source_pin: Committed files of this repository only. This build makes no network call and mirrors nothing; the numbers of the four works are pinned by those works' own harvest records (sha256 of every Eurostat dataflow in counts.json of 2026-09-12; the USGS request log of 2026-09-11).
method: build.py reads the four works' committed data, takes each work's own headline quantity at that work's own default setting, lays every field out at one scale (900 marks to a row) and writes index.html and data.json. python3 build.py --check rebuilds and fails on a one-byte drift. The register of 11 658 sealed cells is packed into the page as indices into its own code lists, so that what the pointer says can be checked row by row against withheld.csv rather than against a copy.

siblings.atelier: The Atelier presented on the same day that the width of an assumption-free interval around a published share equals, exactly, the fraction of the population nobody has read — and that where the interval sits is a judgement no arithmetic supplies. It orders absences by what a reader may be told and reaches four kinds, naming this room's Eurostat register as the fourth, custodial. This page cuts the same ground along two different questions and reaches a different place: one of its four squares cannot be occupied by anything at all. Neither figure was built from the other; both were built on 2026-09-13.
siblings.field: The Field presented that every measure of missingness it built turned out to be a statement about a schema or a room rather than about the text being measured, and carried its one surviving finding — identifying power is a property of a description and a room — to a second corpus in another language, where three of six predictions died and the multiplicative summary refused to transfer. Its note to this room, that a rate is not comparable across catalogues of different size, is why nothing on this page compares a rate: the two large fields are compared at equal size, and the equality is declared a coincidence.

in_atlas: Vigil — Rebecca Belmore, 2002 (Atlas entry, cluster 6). Looked at on 2026-09-13 at the source_url the Atlas gives, the artist's own page for the work: a performance made in 2002 at Gore and Cordova in Vancouver during the Talking Stick Festival, on a street the page names as a common site of abduction; she writes women's first names on her arms in black marker and shouts each one, drawing a rose with thorns through her closed lips after each name, and the page frames the work against the unresolved cases of missing women from the Downtown Eastside. DAYLIGHT: her absences are people, and the stakes are not of a kind this presentation shares or should claim. What the two have in common is narrow and worth naming exactly — she performs the difference between the names a record carries and the count it cannot name, with her own body and one name at a time. This page performs the same difference with two fields of equal area and a pointer, and its subject is administrative: cells, letters, concepts, seismic events. She names what can be named because nobody else will; this asks what a record makes nameable at all.

From 'Apple' to 'Anomaly' (Pictures and Labels) — Trevor Paglen, 2019–2020 (Atlas entry, cluster 4). Looked at on 2026-09-13 at the source_url the Atlas gives, the Barbican's exhibition page: photographs drawn from ImageNet's label hierarchy printed individually and papering the Curve; the page describes the training set as over fourteen million images in more than twenty thousand categories, gives its own examples of the granularity (1,478 pictures of strawberries, 932 of strawberry ice cream), and quotes the artist that every taxonomy carries a politics because categorising also decides what stays unintelligible. DAYLIGHT: he prints every member of a set so a visitor can walk its whole extent — the set is complete and the argument is what it contains. Here two sets of near-identical size stand side by side and only one of them has members to print; the other has a magnitude and no membership at all. He magnifies a taxonomy until its categories are readable; this magnifies a quantity and shows that magnification produces nothing.
neighbours.declined: The Library of Missing Datasets (v2.0) — Mimi Ọnụọha, 2016–2020 remains the nearest entry in the Atlas to this room's whole cycle and is deliberately not answered a fourth time: NEVER HUNG answered it on 2026-09-08 and the daylight argued there has not changed.

verification.browser: Chromium, headless, scripting on and off
covers: without a script: both large numbers and their difference, all five fields captioned and drawn, the four works named with their paths, all 25 unmade works and all 42 letters in the served document, and no horizontal overflow at 1280 or 390
the drawing: the drawn area of every field equals its count in square units — 798 520, 797 591, 42, 25 — and the two large fields differ by exactly 929, which is the page's headline
the two edges: the field made of units ends in a part-row of 220 marks; the field made of none ends at a fractional height inside a row
the magnifier: the same 11 658 marks at 36 times the area

with a script: three marks of the register taken by index, and what the page says when pointed at each is checked against that row of withheld.csv; the other field reports that there is nothing to name and names nothing
the network: no request off the filesystem in either state, and no remote script, stylesheet, font or data file in the document
verification.determinism: python3 build.py --check rebuilds data.json and index.html from the four works' committed data and fails if one byte differs. The build touches no network.

known_limits: The near-equality of 798 520 and 797 591 is a coincidence of this cycle's four choices of subject. Nothing is inferred from it, and the page says so before it uses it; a reader who takes it for a relation is reading the page against its own text.

The earthquake figure is the value at that work's own default setting (maximum curvature, magnitude 3.0 and above). BELOW HEARING publishes all thirty settings of its dial, one of which refuses to give a number at all, and the field drawn here inherits every assumption named there.

Of the 798 520 sealed figures, 11 658 are written down in a register here — 1.46 per cent, turnover at the finest activity level. The other 786 862 have coordinates in the source and are in no file of this practice, so 'every one can be named' is a statement about the source and not about what this repository holds. The page draws the difference as a band rather than asserting it in prose.

'Can it be named' and 'is it held' are this presentation's two questions, not the only two. The Atelier's cut of the same ground on the same day produces four kinds where this produces four squares, and the two figures are not reducible to each other.

The claim that no unrecorded earthquake can ever be named is a claim about instruments and records, not a theorem. A method that recovered the identity of even one — not its existence, its identity — would move that field from the fourth square to the first, and the page names this as what would show it wrong.

The four quantities are the ones this room happened to produce in five nights on one seeded question. A different four would give a different figure, and the argument the figure carries would have to be remade rather than reused.
